children: Nine Licensing Agreements for Transfer of Technology (LAToTS) were handed over to 13 manufacturing partners on Tuesday to enable commercial production of state-of-the-art systems developed by different labs of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).

The technologies — such as advanced underwater naval mine, propellant and igniter to give initial sudden thrust to short range anti-ship missile at launch time, ZnTe (Zinc Telluride) Single Crystal Growth for detection of concealed chemicals and explosives and for wireless communication and Hydro Suit for escape from submarines — have been passed on mostly to the private industry except for a leading State-owned company.

Defence PSU Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL), which will co-produce “multi-influence ground mine” for the  Navy to target modern ships and submarines along with Hyderabad-based Apollo Micro Systems Ltd. Both of these public and private sector companies had also participated in the development process by manufacturing components like electronic systems and resistance outer casing for the mine.

The handing over was done by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh during ‘VIMARSH’, a DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, which unveiled policy initiatives including a comprehensive framework to lower technical and financial entry barriers for MSMEs and deep-tech start-ups, offering direct funding, incubation support and dedicated access to the DRDO testing facilities, the Ministry of Defence said in a statement.

Also present were Defence Secretary RK Singh, who is also holding additional charge as the Chairman of the DRDO and Secretary of the Department of Defence R&D, and other senior officials of MoD, DRDO and senior representatives of private industry.

Three private explosive manufacturing companies — Solar defence & Aerospace Ltd, Premier Explosives Pvt Ltd and Salvo Industries Pvt Ltd — have been opted for production of propellant and igniter for booster and sustainer motors of short range anti-ship missile, which are essential solid rocket propulsion components that generate the required thrust during different flight phases.

Similarly, the DRDO has selected Ananth Technologies Pvt Ltd and Apollo Micro Systems Ltd for the production of semi active homing laser system (SALHS), which is a guidance mechanism widely used in precision-guided munitions (such as laser-guided bombs, missiles, and artillery shells) to strike high-value targets with extreme accuracy.

In some of the cases, the companies have already advanced in the process of manufacturing products. For instance, JCBL Private Ltd had announced in February that the indigenous 20 tonne heavy drop system, developed by the ADRDE lab of DRDO, has been validated by  the Army. The company figured in Tuesday’s announcement of technology transfer for heavy drop system for C-130 Hercules and C-17 Globemaster strategic transporter aircrafts the Indian Air Force operate.

Other selected are: Autotec Systems Pvt Ltd and Accelor Microsystems for electronic activation device that allows operators or onboard fire-control systems to program variable delays, airburst heights, or target-specific detonation profiles prior to launch. Both the companies have also been chosen for wireless control-cum-actuation system to remotely operate, control, and detonate explosive payloads, warheads, or demolition devices.

Billwin Industries Ltd and Uflow Automation will manufacture Hydro Suit, Ants Innovations Pvt Ltd for ZnTe Single Crystal Growth for broadband terahertz applications. Pragati Defence Systems Pvt Ltd has emerged as a production partner for smart helmets.

In his address at the event, Rajnath Singh asserted that the DRDO-Industry collaboration should no longer be limited to production alone, but expanded across the entire value chain encompassing research, design, testing, certification, and manufacturing to transform India into a global hub for defence manufacturing.

Singh underlined that the goal of Viksit Bharat is not merely to build an economically strong nation, but to also make it technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable, and strategically secure. “By 2047, we must achieve Aatmanirbharta in critical technologies, a significant increase in indigenous content, multi-fold growth in defence exports, and a robust presence for India in global supply chains,” he said.

Till date, over 2,300 technology transfers have been handed over to more than 1,100 industries, Defence Secretary RK Singh stated. “Currently, we have made technologies related to approximately 50 missiles, developed by DRDO, available to the industry to foster increased participation,” he added.

A standardised, secure framework for sharing DRDO-developed software source codes with licensee industries was also launched to accelerate software-defined defence capabilities and obsolescence management.

The DRDO also signed a contract with Quality Council of India for System for Advance Manufacturing Assessment and Rating (SAMAR) version 2.0 to benchmark the manufacturing maturity of domestic defence enterprises.

title: DRDO hands over 9 tech transfer agreements to 13 manufacturing partners at ‘VIMARSH’
